TITLE: Duty of Care in Cross-Border Data Breach Litigation
AUTHOR: R. Falconer
SOURCE: (2024) 47 Dalhousie L.J. 205
YEAR: 2024

I. Introduction
Canadian courts have only recently begun to grapple with the duty of care owed by organizations that store personal data across multiple jurisdictions.1

II. Elements of the Duty
A. Proximity
Proximity in the data breach context turns on the relationship between the data custodian and the individuals whose information is at risk.2
B. Foreseeability
Foreseeability is generally uncontroversial once a custodian is aware that it holds sensitive personal information.3

III. Conclusion
A coherent duty of care framework for data breaches would bring welcome predictability to this developing area of Canadian tort law.

1. See generally the discussion in Broutzas v Rouge Valley Health System, 2018 ONSC 6315.
2. Ibid at para 65.
3. Evans v The Bank of Nova Scotia, 2014 ONSC 2135.
